 the task of preventing war is extraordinarily difficult; some might
 say impossible. War is caused by (a) population growth, (b) competition
 for scarce resources, (c) economic greed, (d) racial agendas, (e) the
 "cultural war" and cultural imperialism, (f) religious differences,
 (g) ethnic differences, (h) boredom, (i) desire to "demonstrate" some
 kind of "nobility" or "superiority" on battlefields, (j) disregard for
 the value of human life, (k) insensitivity to individual rights,
 (l)intolerance, (m) conflicting legal systems, (n) arrogance of power,
 (o) willful ignorance, and (p) even Freud's "thanatos" (death wish).
 Of these it is notable how Pyro has exemplified to this newsgroup (a),
 (d), (e), (f), (g), (h), (i), (j), (k), (l), (n), (o), and possibly
 (p), so Pyro has been showing at least 13 of these 16 factors, making
 Pyro to be a rather -dangerous- incendiary component for war-making.

   "Modernism" is a term applied to philosophy, literature, reforms in
 the Catholic Church, and political science, and so has many references
 dependent upon the chosen context.  In general it refers to recasting
 of the notions of "good" and "evil" and methods of truth discovery in
 terms of the perception of alterated circumstances wrought in large
 part by the "industrial revolution" TK identifies in his Manifesto,
 which took place over a period of time extending from the 18th-20th
 centuries.  Modern liberalism, extending from J.S.Mill and others, up
 through Karl Marx, was a pernicious sort of propaganda purposed for
 the goal of managing a growing working class constituting the sector
 of a "labor force" servicing an economy engendered by the industrial
 revolution.  It is false doctrine because J.S.Mill did not apply the
 dialectical methods of Socrates which premised discovery of the Good
 upon first correctly discovering truth.  Neither Hegel nor Marx were
 improvements over Socratic dialectics, but were compromises to the
 Socratic "anti-war" philosophy.  Marx may be read as -satire- of the
 "worldview" offered by the industrial revolution.  Modernism's legacy
 further became Nietzsche and Ayn Rand, each of which offered variants
 to the ancient wisdom which had formerly been -reluctant- to lay any
 claims upon Good and Evil, through (for example) Nietzsche's arrogance
 or Rand's redefinitions.  Many others were also involved in a process
 that corrupted ancient wisdom but are too numerous to list here, and
 they shared a common thread of premising rhetorical methods even as
 they attempted falsely to attire themselves with "dialectics" which
 is a method of inquiry poorly understood since Plato and Aristotle.

   The 20th-century has just recently been picking up the pieces of
 its own legacy that has brought all of history from these past two
 millenia under review, with discoveries in contemporary physics that
 stem from the theories of Einstein, Bohr, Dirac, Planck, Heisenberg,
 Feynman and others, philosophies of Russell, Wittgenstein, C.S.Peirce,
 game-theoretic mathematics of VonNeumann, Conway/Berlekamp/Guy, etc.
 and the subsequent discoveries of software engineering principles with
 computer-development in the latter-half of this 20th-century.  Offered
 to the 21st-century is the "post-modernism" that superceeded modernist
 trends which had culminated with Nietzsche, and also Heidegger to some
 degree, though Heidegger might be said to have straddled modernism and
 post-modernism.  Post-modernism is more further rife with definitional
 problems but may be characterized by "artificial intelligence" and a
 process of disidentification from the past by means of a transcendent
 vision anchored in futurism.  Human history from the time of Aristotle
 and the New Testament, has been for the most part a long struggle in
 darkness which was only recently awakened during the renaissance and
 enlightenment periods, then again submerged by that disaster termed
 the "industrial revolution" accompanied by philosophical modernism
 which was "shocked" back into consciousness following Nietzsche and
 a horrible spectacle of World Wars caused by industrializing arrogance
 throughout Europe, and the "industrial revolution" sent world-wide.
 The "industrial revolution" was not a -political- revolution but a
 period of massive technological change induced by right-wing elements
 with goals essentially being those to exploit the working classes.
 This is the -CAUSE- of much confusion, because in response to that
 (non-political but technological) "industrial revolution" from the
 right, was the "political revolution" from the left called communism.
